summary.text: 岁 is the standardized simplified form of 歲, commonly used for “year” and “age.” The traditional graph’s early formation is disputed; its later seal-script form was analyzed as 步 with 戌 as a sound element.

formation.text: The early graph has competing accounts: some forms are analyzed as 步, meaning walking or movement, with 戉 as a phonetic element; another account proposes that 戉 was borrowed to write the year word and later graphically distinguished. The seal-script graph is analyzed as 步 with phonetic 戌. None establishes a single original construction. The visible parts of 岁 do not independently disclose its origin.

history.text: Accounts report early forms used for “year” and in ritual contexts, with disagreement over their interpretation. Later forms include graphs analyzed with 步; the seal-script form is analyzed as 步 plus 戌. The selected seal-script illustration shows that later form as a modern vector redraw, not an ancient artifact.
岁 is reported as adapted from cursive 歲. The evidence gives this proposed lineage but does not document its specific stages.

uncertainties.text: Early forms may reflect movement plus a sound element, borrowing and later differentiation of 戉, or ritual use. The weapon’s spoken name is not established, so its proposed sound connection to the year word cannot be tested fully. No single original analysis is selected.

senses.period: Oracle-bone period, as reported in supplied paleographic accounts; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: Paleographic accounts report oracle-bone use for “year,” though the graph’s interpretation remains disputed.
The Shuowen entry defines 歲 as Jupiter and describes its circuit through the lunar mansions over twelve months. This historical dictionary sense does not establish the earliest spoken meaning.
“Age” is among the supplied glosses; its emergence and development from earlier uses are not established.

limitations.text: The primary inscriptions and their full contexts were not inspected, so the reported oracle-bone use for “year” and its relation to ritual uses remain provisional.
“Harvest” is listed as a gloss, but its chronology and connection to the other senses are not established.
A calendrical explanation links Jupiter’s roughly twelve-year circuit with “year,” but the evidence does not establish a historical transition between those senses.

overview.text: 岁 is the simplified form of 歲 and commonly means “year”; it is also used for “age.” The traditional graph’s early construction is disputed, so the modern outline alone cannot show its original parts.

relationships.text: 岁 is reported as the standardized simplified counterpart of 歲, adapted from its cursive form; this lineage is not independently confirmed by another supplied source.
